source_row.detail: Assess: a request that is corrupt and names an undeclared data ID is not answered; the InvalidArgument answer to an undeclared data ID is counted and sent under the route's overflow policy; the client-side call ends at its TTL only where no accepted response completes it. Round 2: on a route that does not select the E2E wire, a request whose TTL is 0, one with no payload where its operation requires a value and one of an encoding that no wire declares answered InvalidArgument, once, and counted once; on a route that selects the E2E wire, no request refused before the E2E wire reads it answered. After R2B: the checks of a request in the stated order, each refused request counted once under the first refusing check's cause, also where a result is returned, and an unsent answer counted as an event of its own. After R2C and the Opus pass: answers by the refusing check; no answer to expired or unjudgeable requests; no-header requests counted as unprotected (C05's rule); a caller given a refusal's result gets no means to answer.

source_row.component: the iceoryx2 binding (up-rust SEooC), at any revision; no binding revision was assessed by this correction
source_row.detail: Every arrival is owed a report within the declared latency, but a subscriber at iceoryx2 0.9.3 observes only whether any sample is queued and the samples it takes: no fill count, no eviction event, no refused-arrival event (R1 C2). With a queue that stays non-empty and a failed notification, an arrival has no evidence. The binding needs a mechanism that observes every required arrival at the queue or overflow boundary, or the route's claim is limited as qos and the binding's declaration require; no no-false-miss claim may rest on the subset observed. Two cases make the gap concrete: while one publisher's data connection is missing, arrivals of the route's other publishers into a queue that is already non-empty still need their reports; and a sample that was queued at the previous report, together with a later notification (for example of a publisher whose connection is not yet set up), is no evidence, so the binding needs a way to tell a newly queued sample from an old one.

scopes.purpose: Route every originally unresolved actor scope into an existing or explicitly deferred portfolio without inventing a named implementation owner.

scope_portfolios.remaining_boundary: Crate, binary and supplier/manual scopes remain separate. No coherent Streamer implementation writer is recorded; retain deferral and current SDK interface dependencies.

Tokio, Embassy and scheduler implementation ownership/custody is not established by the inspected metadata. Source9 retains its SDK/shared-interface portions; this does not assign a second SDK writer.
E2E part E6 and its runtime integration remain deferred. Shared SDK receive/builder duties can be recorded separately; no E2E engineering resumes.

The recorded existing XCDR2 implementation and derive need their own source/custody and coherent scope; native/Protobuf ownership does not include them. SDK references do not transfer XCDR2 implementation ownership.

Cortex-M and RISC-V providers require separately identified revisions and implementation custody; RTOS5 is not their owner merely because MCU targets are involved. Source9 owns only its SDK helper/interface portion.
Identify selected host/custom/non-RTOS backend and supported-configuration records. RTOS5 custody remains limited to its recorded MCU/RTOS scope.
Enumerate selected metadata/serialized wires beyond native/Protobuf; a generic wire duty does not select a new wire or authorize its engineering.
Enumerate actual classic UTransport/other binding implementations and revisions; iceoryx2/LoLa are subsets only when the duty applies. No new binding writer is inferred.
Select actual deployment graph, integrator and target/configuration/profile tuples. Deployment duties remain with the integrator, separate from supplier and binding duties.
Close the selected-part roster, including optional/external parts and suppliers. Known component routes do not constitute a complete roster.
